near.diff: 背水の陣 is about fighting with no retreat left; 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず is about choosing danger because the prize lies there.

mean: facing a challenge with no way back, staking everything on it
lit: a battle line drawn up with its back to a river

story.text: Han Xin, a general of the founder of the Han dynasty, attacked the army of Zhao and drew up his troops with a river at their backs, a formation the military manuals warned against. With no way to retreat, his men fought desperately, while a detachment he had sent ahead seized the emptied Zhao camp and raised Han flags. The Zhao army panicked and was crushed.

use.how: Used as a noun, usually 背水の陣で臨む, 背水の陣を敷く or 背水の陣だ, about a decisive challenge where failure leaves no fallback.

near.t: 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず
near.diff: 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず is about choosing danger to win a prize; 背水の陣 is about having cut off every retreat, so you must succeed.

mean: someone who throws their weight around using a powerful backer

story.text: A tiger caught a fox, and the fox said: Heaven has made me king of the beasts, so eating me would defy Heaven; walk behind me and see. Every animal fled at the sight of them, and the tiger, not realising they feared him, believed the fox. A minister of Chu told this to King Xuan to explain that the northern states feared not his official Zhao Xixu but the king's own army that stood behind him.
